summary: Verified plan v3 of case-onboarding (design-only, 5 milestones, 22 steps, 2 blocked, 120 acceptance tests) on all three lenses and rejected it. Executability 21/22, grounding 22/22, testability 12/22. Thirteen blockers and twelve warnings. All 45 declared checker tests were run verbatim against fixtures built from the cited skills' metadata examples, at the scope each test declares: 39 exit 0 on correct artefacts, six cannot exit 0 on any artefact set this plan declares. The plan's mechanics are clean — validate exits 0 with the same six warnings before and after this run, no output collides, the dependency graph is acyclic, every requirement reaches a tested step, and every decision-tree branch quote matched its tree verbatim. What fails is the test surface and one output ownership: five of the six failing checkers are the same four failure modes the planner found and fixed elsewhere in v3 but did not sweep for, and M4-S05 declares a package.xml apex-builder does not produce. Two milestone gates (M2, M3) are additionally unreachable, because a manual test whose tick is deferred to M5 stops its step reaching 'documented'.
confidence_rationale: All three lenses ran on all 22 steps and every verdict names a file read or a command run. MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the grounding lens's 'gotchas not contradicted' and 'questions answered' checks were made by targeted reading of the skills each defect touched plus the checkers that encode those gotchas, not by opening all 33 cited skills' gotchas files and Questions tables; and because the fixtures are this agent's reconstruction of correct artefacts, so a checker that passed could still fail on what the builder actually writes. Not LOW: build_plan.py and the schema were available, no refutation rests on a missing file, and every blocker rests on a reproduced command output rather than on absence.

All 33 cited skills resolve, all 3 cited templates and all 7 cited decision-tree files exist, D10's treeless decision carries a source_reference that resolves, and all nine tree-grounded branch quotes were found verbatim in the trees they cite — not paraphrased.

Five of this round's blockers are the same four failure modes one step over: a checker that exits non-zero on a correct artefact (M2-S02, M3-S02, M5-S05 — the X01/X03 pattern), a checker vacuous at step scope (M4-S02 — the X05/W07 pattern), and a description asserting a cross-reference the scope cannot see (M2-S03 — the W03 pattern).

process_observations.observation: The contract says two things about a checker's scope that this plan makes collide. Section 5 says the tester 'executes a declared checker command verbatim ... no path is substituted', while build-plan.schema.json says scope 'step' means the checker runs over artefacts/<step-id>/. M5-S04's RTM test declares no scope and passes --manifest-dir artefacts, so which of the two governs is undefined. It is recorded as a blocker on the instruction that the two must agree, but the underlying ambiguity is the contract's.
